ESV.1: Now the boy Samuel was ministering to the LORD in the presence of Eli. And the word of the LORD was rare in those days; there was no frequent vision.
ESV.2: At that time Eli, whose eyesight had begun to grow dim so that he could not see, was lying down in his own place.
ESV.3: The lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was.
ESV.4: Then the LORD called Samuel, and he said, “Here I am!”
ESV.5: and ran to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” But he said, “I did not call; lie down again.” So he went and lay down.
ESV.6: And the LORD called again, “Samuel!” and Samuel arose and went to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” But he said, “I did not call, my son; lie down again.”
ESV.7: Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, and the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him.
ESV.8: And the LORD called Samuel again the third time. And he arose and went to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” Then Eli perceived that the LORD was calling the boy.
ESV.9: Therefore Eli said to Samuel, “Go, lie down, and if he calls you, you shall say, ‘Speak, LORD, for your servant hears.’” So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
ESV.10: And the LORD came and stood, calling as at other times, “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel said, “Speak, for your servant hears.”
ESV.11: Then the LORD said to Samuel, “Behold, I am about to do a thing in Israel at which the two ears of everyone who hears it will tingle.
ESV.12: On that day I will fulfill against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from beginning to end.
ESV.13: And I declare to him that I am about to punish his house forever, for the iniquity that he knew, because his sons were blaspheming God,  and he did not restrain them.
ESV.14: Therefore I swear to the house of Eli that the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be atoned for by sacrifice or offering forever.”
ESV.15: Samuel lay until morning; then he opened the doors of the house of the LORD. And Samuel was afraid to tell the vision to Eli.
ESV.16: But Eli called Samuel and said, “Samuel, my son.” And he said, “Here I am.”
ESV.17: And Eli said, “What was it that he told you? Do not hide it from me. May God do so to you and more also if you hide anything from me of all that he told you.”
ESV.18: So Samuel told him everything and hid nothing from him. And he said, “It is the LORD. Let him do what seems good to him.”
ESV.19: And Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him and let none of his words fall to the ground.
ESV.20: And all Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established as a prophet of the LORD.
ESV.21: And the LORD appeared again at Shiloh, for the LORD revealed himself to Samuel at Shiloh by the word of the LORD.

NASB.1: Now the boy Samuel was ministering to the LORD before Eli. And word from the LORD was rare in those days, visions were infrequent.

NASB.3: and the lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD where the ark of God [was],
NASB.4: that the LORD called Samuel; and he said, 'Here I am.'
NASB.5: Then he ran to Eli and said, 'Here I am, for you called me.' But he said, 'I did not call, lie down again.' So he went and lay down.
NASB.6: The LORD called yet again, 'Samuel!' So Samuel arose and went to Eli and said, 'Here I am, for you called me.' But he answered, 'I did not call, my son, lie down again.'
NASB.7: Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, nor had the word of the LORD yet been revealed to him.
NASB.8: So the LORD called Samuel again for the third time. And he arose and went to Eli and said, 'Here I am, for you called me.' Then Eli discerned that the LORD was calling the boy.
NASB.9: And Eli said to Samuel, 'Go lie down, and it shall be if He calls you, that you shall say, 'Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.'' So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
NASB.10: Then the LORD came and stood and called as at other times, 'Samuel! Samuel!' And Samuel said, 'Speak, for Your servant is listening.'
NASB.11: The LORD said to Samuel, 'Behold, I am about to do a thing in Israel at which both ears of everyone who hears it will tingle.
NASB.12: 'In that day I will carry out against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from beginning to end.
NASB.13: 'For I have told him that I am about to judge his house forever for the iniquity which he knew, because his sons brought a curse on themselves and he did not rebuke them.
NASB.14: 'Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be atoned for by sacrifice or offering forever.'
NASB.15: So Samuel lay down until morning. Then he opened the doors of the house of the LORD. But Samuel was afraid to tell the vision to Eli.
NASB.16: Then Eli called Samuel and said, 'Samuel, my son.' And he said, 'Here I am.'
NASB.17: He said, 'What is the word that He spoke to you? Please do not hide it from me. May God do so to you, and more also, if you hide anything from me of all the words that He spoke to you.'
NASB.18: So Samuel told him everything and hid nothing from him. And he said, 'It is the LORD; let Him do what seems good to Him.'
NASB.19: Thus Samuel grew and the LORD was with him and let none of his words fail.
NASB.20: All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet of the LORD.
NASB.21: And the LORD appeared again at Shiloh, because the LORD revealed Himself to Samuel at Shiloh by the word of the LORD.

CSB17.1: The boy Samuel served the LORD in Eli’s presence. <sup>ⓐ</sup> In those days the word of the LORD was rare and prophetic visions were not widespread. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.2: One day Eli, whose eyesight was failing, <sup>ⓒ</sup> was lying in his usual place.
CSB17.3: Before the lamp of God had gone out, <sup>ⓓ</sup> Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was located.
CSB17.4: Then the LORD called Samuel, <sup>[1]</sup> and he answered, “Here I am.”
CSB17.5: He ran to Eli and said, “Here I am; you called me.” “I didn’t call,” Eli replied. “Go back and lie down.” So he went and lay down.
CSB17.6: Once again the LORD called, “Samuel!” Samuel got up, went to Eli, and said, “Here I am; you called me.” “I didn’t call, my son,” he replied. “Go back and lie down.”
CSB17.7: Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, because the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him.
CSB17.8: Once again, for the third time, the LORD called Samuel. He got up, went to Eli, and said, “Here I am; you called me.” Then Eli understood that the LORD was calling the boy.
CSB17.9: He told Samuel, “Go and lie down. If he calls you, say, ‘Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening.’” So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
CSB17.10: The LORD came, stood there, and called as before, “Samuel, Samuel!” Samuel responded, “Speak, for your servant is listening.”
CSB17.11: The LORD said to Samuel, “I am about to do something in Israel that everyone who hears about it will shudder. <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.12: On that day I will carry out against Eli everything I said about his family, from beginning to end. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.13: I told him that I am going to judge his family forever because of the iniquity he knows about: his sons are cursing God, <sup>[3]</sup> and he has not stopped them. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.14: Therefore, I have sworn to Eli’s family: The iniquity of Eli’s family will never be wiped out by either sacrifice or offering.” <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.15: Samuel lay down until the morning; then he opened the doors of the LORD’s house. He was afraid to tell Eli the vision,
CSB17.16: but Eli called him and said, “Samuel, my son.” “Here I am,” answered Samuel.
CSB17.17: “What was the message he gave you?” Eli asked. “Don’t hide it from me. May God punish you and do so severely if you hide anything from me that he told you.” <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.18: So Samuel told him everything and did not hide anything from him. Eli responded, “He is the LORD. Let him do what he thinks is good.” <sup>[4]</sup> <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.19: Samuel grew, <sup>ⓚ</sup> and the LORD was with him, <sup>ⓛ</sup> and he fulfilled everything Samuel prophesied. <sup>[5]</sup> <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.20: All Israel from Dan to Beer-sheba knew that Samuel was a confirmed prophet of the LORD. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.21: The LORD continued to appear in Shiloh, because there he revealed himself to Samuel by his word. <sup>ⓐ</sup>

AMP.1: Now the boy Samuel was attending to the service of the LORD under the supervision of Eli. The word of the LORD was rare and precious in those days; visions [that is, new revelations of divine truth] were not widespread.
AMP.2: Yet it happened at that time, as Eli was lying down in his own place (now his eyesight had begun to grow dim and he could not see well).
AMP.3: and the [oil] lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was,
AMP.4: that the LORD called Samuel, and he answered, "Here I am."
AMP.5: He ran to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." But Eli said, "I did not call you; lie down again." So he went and lay down.
AMP.6: Then the LORD called yet again, "Samuel!" So Samuel got up and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." But Eli answered, "I did not call, my son; lie down again."
AMP.7: Now Samuel did not yet know [or personally experience] the LORD, and the word of the LORD was not yet revealed [directly] to him.
AMP.8: So the LORD called Samuel a third time. And he stood and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you did call me." Then Eli understood that it was the LORD [who was] calling the boy.
AMP.9: So Eli said to Samuel, "Go, lie down, and it shall be that if He calls you, you shall say, 'Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.'" So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
AMP.10: Then the LORD came and stood and called as at the previous times, "Samuel! Samuel!" Then Samuel answered, "Speak, for Your servant is listening."
AMP.11: The LORD said to Samuel, "Behold, I am about to do a thing in Israel at which both ears of everyone who hears it will ring.
AMP.12: On that day I will carry out against Eli everything that I have spoken concerning his house (family), from beginning to end.
AMP.13: Now I have told him that I am about to judge his house forever for the sinful behavior which he knew [was happening], because his sons were bringing a curse on themselves [dishonoring and blaspheming God] and he did not rebuke them.
AMP.14: Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the sinful behavior of Eli's house (family) shall not be atoned for by sacrifice or offering forever."
AMP.15: So Samuel lay down until morning. Then he opened the doors of the <e>Lord's</e> house. But Samuel was afraid to tell the vision to Eli.
AMP.16: But Eli called Samuel and said, "Samuel, my son." And he answered, "Here I am."
AMP.17: Then Eli said, "What is it that He said to you? Please do not hide it from me. May God do the same to you, and more also, if you hide from me anything of all that He said to you."
AMP.18: So Samuel told him everything, hiding nothing from him. And Eli said, "It is the LORD; may He do what seems good to Him."
AMP.19: Now Samuel grew; and the LORD was with him and He let none of his words fail [to be fulfilled].
AMP.20: And all Israel from Dan [in the north] to Beersheba [in the south] knew that Samuel was appointed as a prophet of the LORD.
AMP.21: And the LORD continued to appear in Shiloh, for the LORD revealed Himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the LORD.

NLT.1: Meanwhile, the boy Samuel served the LORD by assisting Eli. Now in those days messages from the LORD were very rare, and visions were quite uncommon.
NLT.2: One night Eli, who was almost blind by now, had gone to bed.
NLT.3: The lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was sleeping in the Tabernacle near the Ark of God.
NLT.4: Suddenly the LORD called out, “Samuel!” “Yes?” Samuel replied. “What is it?”
NLT.5: He got up and ran to Eli. “Here I am. Did you call me?” “I didn’t call you,” Eli replied. “Go back to bed.” So he did.
NLT.6: Then the LORD called out again, “Samuel!” Again Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am. Did you call me?” “I didn’t call you, my son,” Eli said. “Go back to bed.”
NLT.7: Samuel did not yet know the LORD because he had never had a message from the LORD before.
NLT.8: So the LORD called a third time, and once more Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am. Did you call me?” Then Eli realized it was the LORD who was calling the boy.
NLT.9: So he said to Samuel, “Go and lie down again, and if someone calls again, say, ‘Speak, LORD, your servant is listening.’” So Samuel went back to bed.
NLT.10: And the LORD came and called as before, “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel replied, “Speak, your servant is listening.”
NLT.11: Then the LORD said to Samuel, “I am about to do a shocking thing in Israel.
NLT.12: I am going to carry out all my threats against Eli and his family, from beginning to end.
NLT.13: I have warned him that judgment is coming upon his family forever, because his sons are blaspheming God and he hasn’t disciplined them.
NLT.14: So I have vowed that the sins of Eli and his sons will never be forgiven by sacrifices or offerings.”

MSG.1: The boy Samuel was serving God under Eli's direction. This was at a time when the revelation of God was rarely heard or seen.
MSG.2: One night Eli was sound asleep (his eyesight was very bad—he could hardly see).
MSG.3: It was well before dawn; the sanctuary lamp was still burning. Samuel was still in bed in the Temple of God, where the Chest of God rested.
MSG.4:
Then God called out, "Samuel, Samuel!"
Samuel answered, "Yes? I'm here."
MSG.5:
Then he ran to Eli saying, "I heard you call. Here I am."
Eli said, "I didn't call you. Go back to bed." And so he did.
MSG.6:
God called again, "Samuel, Samuel!"
Samuel got up and went to Eli, "I heard you call. Here I am."
Again Eli said, "Son, I didn't call you. Go back to bed."
MSG.7: (This all happened before Samuel knew God for himself. It was before the revelation of God had been given to him personally.)
MSG.8:
God called again, "Samuel!"—the third time! Yet again Samuel got up and went to Eli, "Yes? I heard you call me. Here I am."
That's when it dawned on Eli that God was calling the boy.
MSG.9: So Eli directed Samuel, "Go back and lie down. If the voice calls again, say, 'Speak, God. I'm your servant, ready to listen.' " Samuel returned to his bed.
MSG.10:
Then God came and stood before him exactly as before, calling out, "Samuel! Samuel!"
Samuel answered, "Speak. I'm your servant, ready to listen."
MSG.11: God said to Samuel, "Listen carefully. I'm getting ready to do something in Israel that is going to shake everyone up and get their attention.
MSG.12: The time has come for me to bring down on Eli's family everything I warned him of, every last word of it.
MSG.13: I'm letting him know that the time's up. I'm bringing judgment on his family for good. He knew what was going on, that his sons were desecrating God's name and God's place, and he did nothing to stop them.
MSG.14: This is my sentence on the family of Eli: The evil of Eli's family can never be wiped out by sacrifice or offering."
MSG.15: Samuel stayed in bed until morning, then rose early and went about his duties, opening the doors of the sanctuary, but he dreaded having to tell the vision to Eli.
MSG.16:
But then Eli summoned Samuel: "Samuel, my son!"
Samuel came running: "Yes? What can I do for you?"
MSG.17: "What did he say? Tell it to me, all of it. Don't suppress or soften one word, as God is your judge! I want it all, word for word as he said it to you."
MSG.18:
So Samuel told him, word for word. He held back nothing.
Eli said, "He is God. Let him do whatever he thinks best."
MSG.19: Samuel grew up. God was with him, and Samuel's prophetic record was flawless.
MSG.20: Everyone in Israel, from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, recognized that Samuel was the real thing—a true prophet of God.
MSG.21: God continued to show up at Shiloh, revealed through his word to Samuel at Shiloh.

NET.1: Now the boy Samuel continued serving the LORD under Eli’s supervision. Word from the LORD was rare in those days; revelatory visions were infrequent.
NET.2: Eli’s eyes had begun to fail, so that he was unable to see well. At that time he was lying down in his place,
NET.3: and the lamp of God had not yet been extinguished. Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD as well; the ark of God was also there.
NET.4: The LORD called to Samuel, and he replied, “Here I am!”
NET.5: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” But Eli said, “I didn’t call you. Go back and lie down.” So he went back and lay down.
NET.6: The LORD again called, “Samuel!” So Samuel got up and went to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” But Eli said, “I didn’t call you, my son. Go back and lie down.”
NET.7: Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD; the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him.
NET.8: Then the LORD called Samuel a third time. So he got up and went to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you called me!” Eli then realized that it was the LORD who was calling the boy.
NET.9: So Eli said to Samuel, “Go back and lie down. When he calls you, say, “Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening.” So Samuel went back and lay down in his place.
NET.10: Then the LORD came and stood nearby, calling as he had previously done, “Samuel! Samuel!” Samuel replied, “Speak, for your servant is listening!”
NET.11: The LORD said to Samuel, “Look! I am about to do something in Israel; when anyone hears about it, both of his ears will tingle.
NET.12: On that day I will carry out against Eli everything that I spoke about his house — from start to finish!
NET.13: You should tell him that I am about to judge his house forever because of the sin that he knew about. For his sons were cursing God, and he did not rebuke them.
NET.14: Therefore I swore an oath to the house of Eli, ‘The sin of the house of Eli can never be forgiven by sacrifice or by grain offering.’”
NET.15: So Samuel lay down until morning. Then he opened the doors of the LORD’s house. But Samuel was afraid to tell Eli about the vision.
NET.16: However, Eli called Samuel and said, “Samuel, my son!” He replied, “Here I am.”
NET.17: Eli said, “What message did he speak to you? Don’t conceal it from me. God will judge you severely if you conceal from me anything that he said to you!”
NET.18: So Samuel told him everything. He did not hold back anything from him. Eli said, “The LORD will do what he pleases.”
NET.19: Samuel continued to grow, and the LORD was with him. None of his prophecies fell to the ground unfulfilled.
NET.20: All Israel from Dan to Beer Sheba realized that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet of the LORD.
NET.21: Then the LORD again appeared in Shiloh, for it was in Shiloh that the LORD had revealed himself to Samuel through the word of the LORD.
